equivalence_table.what_this_is: Grammar forms that are interchangeable in the same blank. build_exam_banks.py never offers a member of a class as a distractor when the key is another member of the same class and the class context matches: gf:n4:3535 「これはお茶（　）味だ。」 keyed のような offered みたいな, which is just as correct. Read by scripts/export/exam_rules.py (load_equivalents / interchangeable).
equivalence_table.rule: Two options are interchangeable when both are in one class's `forms` and the class context holds. `before` (optional) is a regex that must match the END of the text before the blank; `after` (optional) is a regex that must match the START of the text after it. A class with no context applies everywhere. Classes list exact option strings; a form reaches the option pool only through grammar_point.forms_json, so a member that no level attests is inert until it is.

derivation.method: Candidates came from the grammar registry, then each class was checked against the 944 gf/tg items. Mechanical signals (scratch derive.py): (1) en form_meanings identical once the register tag is stripped; (2) spellings named in a point's own label; (3) W08 / W08b merge pairs. Classes with no mechanical signal quote the owning points' form_meanings in `evidence`. A context (`before` / `after`) was added wherever a naive class would have flagged a valid item, e.g. でも is 'but' only sentence-initially (gf:n5:4278 ...んだ（　） keyed けど, でも offered, stays valid).
derivation.label_alternations_not_used: ちゃった/じゃった, とく/どく, とおり/どおり, おう/よう and になる/くなる are allomorphs chosen by the preceding sound, never both right in one blank, so they are not classes (じゃった pairs with でしまった instead).
derivation.merge_pairs_note: A merge pair shares a key after the merge, so the same-point rule already covers it; the ledgers mattered for the classes they expose across points (gp-77 / gp-76 / gp-153 like-forms, te-shimau-chau's ちゃう).

vocab_scan.method: kr: distractor is a JMdict or vocab_form reading of the printed stem. or: distractor spelling reads as the printed kana in JMdict, or is another spelling of the key's own entry. cf: distractor (by printed spelling, every record) shares a pt-BR sense-0 gloss with the key, or is another spelling of the key's entry. Equal first gloss (pt-BR or en) was flagged in every family.

informational_not_defects.verdict: not a second answer: ひかり (光) and 明かり share the gloss 'luz / light', but 明かり cannot be read ひかり: a same-meaning reading is the kind of distractor a reading item wants.
not a second answer: pt-BR 'direção' is both 運転 (driving) and 方向 (direction); the en glosses differ and 運転 is never read ほうこう.
not a second answer: われる (割れる) and 折れる both gloss 'quebrar / to break', but 折れる is never read われる.
not a second answer: pt-BR 'partida' is both 出発 (departure) and 試合 (match); 試合 is never spelled しゅっぱつ.
not a second answer: 大きな is a different word (adnominal); おおきな does not read 大きい and its tail な does not match the printed い.

vocab_scan.limits: cf was not read item by item: a semantic fit with no gloss overlap would not surface here.

context_underdetermined.what: Not equivalents, so the table cannot and should not catch them: the distractor means something else, but the stem gives no context that rules it out (gf:n5:4292 is the bare stem 「（　）？」). Judged by one reader while reading every gf/tg item; the teacher loop decides. Mechanical levers, not in this patch: a minimum of stem content outside the blank; refusing a distractor that attaches to the same stem shape as the key (た/て-forms after a する or ichidan stem, e.g. gf:n4:3509-3513 たらいいですか vs たらどうですか).
